standard_prerequisites.use: The universally bounded stratification lemma (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-lqf-universally-bounded, same chapter) and the finite-stage descent of finite locally free morphisms (Limits, lemma-descend-finite-locally-free).

core_obligations: Bound the fibre cardinalities universally and invoke the bounded stratification.
Prove quasi-compactness of strata by cutting the defining ideal to finitely many generators.

proof_roadmap.step: Universal boundedness reduces existence to the stratification lemma.
Descent of finite locally free-ness to a finitely generated stage makes strata quasi-compact.

difficulty_reason: For f : X -> S flat, locally of finite presentation, separated and quasi-finite, the lemma builds closed subsets Z_{-1} empty contained in Z_0 contained in Z_1 ... in S such that S_r = Z_r minus Z_{r-1} is the locus where the projection X x_S T -> T is finite locally free of degree r exactly when the map factors set-theoretically through S_r, and moreover each inclusion S_r -> S is quasi-compact. The retained proof is written in two paragraphs: existence uses universal boundedness of the fibres (Morphisms, lemma-locally-quasi-finite-qc-source-universally-bounded) feeding the chapter's bounded-degree stratification lemma; quasi-compactness of the strata is shown by proving each difference U_r -> U_{r-1} quasi-compact through a descent argument where the ideal of the closed stratum is cut down to a finitely generated ideal via Limits, lemma-descend-finite-locally-free, making the complement a finite union of standard opens. Retained author proof at lines 12861-12889.
